HOW THE PROPHECY AGREES WITH THE GOSPEL, CONCERNING THE DARKENING OF THE SUN AND CERTAIN OTHER THINGS. — Since at the Lord’s first coming it was foretold that the sun would be darkened at his passion, at the very hour when it is proved to have happened, that is, at midday, for therefore it is written in the prophet Amos: “And it shall come to pass in that day, says the Lord, I will cause the sun to go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the clear day” (Amos 8:9). On that day, therefore, from the sixth hour the sun was darkened until the ninth hour, and therefore the prophecy of the aforementioned prophet was fulfilled. The image of this event, which is to occur at the Lord’s second coming, was shown in the Lord’s passion; […]

8:9.t: And it shall be in that day, says the Lord: The sun shall set at midday, and I will make the earth grow dark in the day of light; and I will turn your festivals into mourning and all your songs into lamentation; and I will bring sackcloth upon every back of yours and baldness upon every head; and I will make it like the mourning for an only son, and its last end like a bitter day. LXX: And it shall be in that day, says the Lord God: The sun shall set at midday, and the light shall grow dark upon the earth in the day; and I will turn your solemnities into mourning and all your songs into lamentation; and I will bring sackcloth upon every loin and baldness upon every head; and I will make it like the mourning for a beloved one, and those who are with him like a day of grief. […]

And some are commanded to "be angry" after a wholesome fashion, but with our own selves, and with evil thoughts that arise, and "not to sin," viz., by bringing them to a bad issue. Finally, the next verse explains this to be the meaning more clearly: "The things you say in your hearts, be sorry for them on your beds:" i.e., whatever you think of in your hearts when sudden and nervous excitements rush in on you, correct and amend with wholesome sorrow, lying as it were on a bed of rest, and removing by the moderating influence of counsel all noise and disturbance of wrath. Lastly, the blessed Apostle, when he made use of the testimony of this verse, and said, "Be ye angry and sin not," added, "Let not the sun go down upon your wrath, neither give place to the devil." […]
8:9.s: The Twelve Books on the Institutes of the Coenobia, Book 8, Chapters 9-10

8:9.t: In relation to Christ's death, it is said: "The sun shall go down at midday." At midday, the sun falls for the Jews. When Christ was at the highest point of His power, that is, after the resurrection and the ascension, the Jews were blinded.

8:10.t:
This prophecy was thus fulfilled, and it goes on to say:

"And I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your song into lamentation. And I will bring sackcloth on all loins, and baldness on every head: And I will make him as grief for a dear one, and them with him as a day of pain. Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will send famine upon the earth, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the word of the Lord," etc.

And all this prophecy of what would result from their insolence against the Christ has been clearly proved to have taken place after their plot against our Saviour. […]
8:10.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 10, Chapter 6

8:10.t: They, instead of a belt, are girded with ropes and haircloth; to us, with the apostles, it is said: Let your loins be girded, and burning lamps in your hands. We are girded with the truth of Christ, fulfilling what is written: Stand, having your loins girded in truth. But they, instead of truth, are girt about with the lie of the devil. Our head, of which the Savior speaks: But even the hairs of your head are numbered, has perpetual hair, and in our head, who is Christ, we possess strength to kill the lion. […]

8:11.t: But this also, which he says, "about thirty years old", must be considered. "Joseph was thirty years old" when he was released from his chains and, having interpreted the dream of Pharaoh, was made ruler of Egypt, and in the time of plenty gathered wheat, so that in the time of famine he might have what he could distribute. I think that the thirty years of Joseph went before, as a type of the thirty years of the Savior. For this Joseph gathered not such wheat as that Joseph in Egypt, but true and heavenly wheat, so that, the wheat having been gathered in the time of plenty, he might have what he could distribute when famine had been sent into Egypt, "not a famine of bread nor a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the word of God". […]
8:11.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 28

8:11.t: For you indeed supply bodily food to peoples and cities so far as your lovingkindness reaches; and you supply spiritual food also, not to a particular people, nor to this or that city, circumscribed by narrow boundaries, though its people may think it very illustrious, but to almost the whole world. And you bring the remedy not for famine of bread or thirst of water, which is no very terrible famine—and to avoid it is easy; but to a famine of hearing the Word of the Lord, which it is most miserable to suffer, and a most laborious matter to cure at the present time, because iniquity hath abounded, and scarce anywhere do I find its genuine healers.

Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and I will send a famine into the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the word of the Lord. And they shall be moved from sea to sea, and from the north to the east they shall go about seeking the word of the Lord, and shall not find it. In that day the beautiful virgins shall fail, and the young men, in thirst, who swear by the sin of Samaria, and say: Your god lives, Dan, and the way of Beersheba lives; and they shall fall and shall not rise again any longer. LXX: Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord God, and I will send forth a famine upon the land, not a famine of bread nor a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the word of the Lord. […]

But the Lord sends a famine into the land upon those who savor earthly things; and a famine not of bread, and a thirst not of water, but of hearing the word of the Lord, when on account of the sins of the people teaching fails in the churches; and from sea to sea, that is, from salt and most bitter waves they come as far as the sea; not meeting with rivers, nor with most sweet and varied springs, but running back again to bitter things; and from the north to the east, desiring to forsake the north, which is the harshest wind and is called 'the right-hand wind' by the ignorant, and to reach the east, which they will not be able to find, because they do not go by a straight road but wander about by devious paths, and, not keeping to the king's road, are led along winding turns.

8:13.t: In that time the beautiful virgins failed, and the young men, or the chosen ones and teachers — for this is what baurim means —, failed in thirst. They interpret the beautiful virgins as the synagogues, and the chosen ones as the masters of the people. And since these have failed, they teach that the curses of Deuteronomy have been fulfilled in the Jewish people.

In that time the virgin souls will fail, which the Apostle calls uncorrupted; and he desires them to possess everlasting chastity, writing to the Corinthians: For I betrothed you to one husband, to present a chaste virgin to Christ. But I fear lest, as the serpent seduced Eve by his cunning, so your minds should be corrupted and fall away from the simplicity which is in Christ. And if all virgins were beautiful or good, he would never have said: The good virgins will fail; but he set down 'good' to distinguish them from bad virgins, the good being those who are holy in body and in spirit. The bad virgins are the five foolish ones, who did not prepare oil for their lamps. The good and comely virgins are those who had the light of the virtues and entered the bridegroom's chamber. […]

And when the virgins fail, the young men too will fail, who had previously conquered the world; and they will fail for this reason, because they swear by the idol of Samaria, which we always take as standing for the heretics, as this same prophet says: Woe to those who despise Zion, and trust in the mountain of Samaria. For the heretics despise the Church of the Lord and trust in the falsity of their own dogmas, raising themselves up against the knowledge of God, having split his people, and saying: We have no portion in David, nor inheritance in the son of Jesse. If anyone, therefore, swears by the sin of Samaria and says: Your god lives, Dan, and the way of Beersheba lives, he will fall and will not be able to rise again any longer. […]

8:14.t: These chosen ones and teachers swore by the idol of Samaria, that is, by the golden calves, and said: Your god lives, Dan, at the borders of the land of Judea, where Paneas now is, and where at that time the golden calf was worshipped, and the way of Beersheba lives, because they travelled there by a long and seldom-taken journey, on account of the kings of Judah, the righteous and the unrighteous alike. And because they did this, they will therefore fall and will not rise again any more, that is, they will not recover the state which they had had before.

9:1.t: This I take from the work of Josephus on Jewish Antiquities. And I found in the beginning of the Prophet Amos the statement that he began to prophesy "in the days of Ozias, king of Judah, two years before the earthquake." What earthquake he does not clearly say. But I think the same prophet further on suggests this earthquake, when he says: "I saw the Lord standing on the altar. And He said, Strike the altar, and the doors shall be shaken, and strike the heads of all, and the remnant I will slay with the sword." […]
9:1.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 6, Chapter 18

9:1.t: I saw the Lord standing upon the altar, and he said: Strike the hinge, and let the lintels be shaken; for avarice is at the head of them all, and the last of them I will slay with the sword. There shall be no flight for them; whoever of these flees shall flee and shall not be saved. LXX: I saw the Lord standing upon the altar, and he said: Strike upon the mercy seat, and the porches shall be shaken; and dash apart upon the heads of all, and the rest of them I will slay with the sword. Whoever of them flees shall not flee away; and whoever of them has been saved again shall not be saved. […]

9:2.t: If they go down even to hell, from there my hand shall bring them out; and if they go up even into heaven, from there I will drag them down; and if they are hidden on the top of Carmel, from there I will search them out and take them away; and if they hide themselves from my eyes in the depth of the sea, there I will command the serpent, and it shall bite them; and if they go into captivity before their enemies, there I will command the sword, and it shall slay them; and I will set my eyes upon them for evil, and not for good. And the Lord God of hosts, who touches the earth and it melts, and all who dwell in it shall mourn, and the whole of it shall rise up like a stream, and shall flow down like the river of Egypt. […]

And these things, following the order of the history, we have interpreted as best we could, if indeed understanding has not failed us in some points. But David sets out the whole περιοχὴν (the whole tenor) of this passage, saying: Lord, you have proved me, and you have known me. And at once he adds: Where shall I go from your spirit, and from your face where shall I flee? If I ascend into heaven, you are there; if I descend into hell, you are there. If I take my wings at dawn, and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea: even there your hand shall lead me, and your right hand shall hold me. […]

9:3.t: [Daniel 7:2-3] "And during the night I saw in my vision, and behold, the four winds of heaven strove upon the great sea, and four great beasts were coming up out of the sea, differing from one another." The four winds of heaven I suppose to have been angelic powers to whom the principalities have been committed, in accordance with what we read in Deuteronomy: "When the Most High divided the nations and when He separated the children of Adam, He established the bounds of the peoples according to the number of the angels. For the Lord's portion is His people; Jacob is the line of His inheritance (Deuteronomy 32:8). […]

If they are hidden on the top of Carmel, either by the borders of Phoenicia in the northern region, or toward the south on account of the vastness of the desert, where Nabal of Carmel once lived, from there, he says, I will search them out and take them away; and if in the depth of the sea, and, to speak of the prophet, in Tarshish, they try to avoid the eyes of God, there I will command the serpent, by which in this place he signifies Leviathan, or the sea-monster, so as to keep the metaphor, and to come to the enemies by way of the serpent and the sea-monster. And it shall bite them, that is, it shall devour them with its jaws.

9:4.t: And lest perhaps, from what he said above, we should understand anything other than captivity at the hands of the enemy, Scripture, after its custom, has disclosed what it had said before under riddles. And if they go into captivity before their enemies, there I will command the sword, and it shall slay them: so that, namely, they may not think servitude the extremity of their evils, but the enemy's blade may pierce them even as captives; and those who have been able to survive and escape death may not escape the gaze of God, but he will set his eyes upon them for evil and not for good, so that he may always visit them and drive them to repentance through torments.

9:5.t: And Almighty God says that he will do these things, at whose touch and nod the foundations of the earth are shaken, or melt, and every inhabitant of it is taken up with lamentation and mourning. He says these things to show the greatness of the divine power, lest perhaps he should indeed wish to do what he threatens, but his strength should not fulfil his will. But if the earth melts, or is shaken, and even insensible nature feels its Creator, how much more man, a fragile creature, the treasure of whose soul is shut up in earthen and bodily vessels? And as the river of Egypt runs down into the sea and is swallowed up, so also the land of Israel, of which he had said above: Who touches the earth and it melts, will go into captivity and will be devoured by the enemies; […]

9:6.t: The heavenly intelligences gazed with admiration on "the Jerusalem that is above," and by the mouth of Isaiah said long ago, "Who are these that fly as clouds, and as doves with their young ones, unto me?" Now, as Christ has prepared for us this ascension into heaven, he must be the Christ of whom Amos spoke: "It is he who builds his ascent up to the heavens," even for himself and his people.

He who builds his ascent in heaven, and has founded his bundle upon the earth; who calls the waters of the sea, and pours them out upon the face of the earth: the Lord is his name. LXX: He who builds his ascent in heaven, and founds his promise upon the earth; who calls the water of the sea, and pours it out upon the face of the earth: the Lord Almighty is his name. The Lord God Almighty, who looks upon, or touches, the earth and shakes it, is himself the one who daily builds his ascent into heaven, and says in the Gospel: My Father works until now, and I work. And not only did he once build Eve from the rib of Adam as a type of the Church, but daily he builds believers and the members of his body, and lifts them from the earth to heaven, so that in them he himself may climb up. […]

9:7.t: Are you not like the sons of the Ethiopians to me, sons of Israel, says the Lord? Did I not make Israel go up from the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Cappadocia, and the Syrians from Cyrene? Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the sinning kingdom, and I will crush it from the face of the earth; nevertheless, crushing, I will not crush the house of Jacob, says the Lord. LXX: Are you not like the sons of the Ethiopians to me, sons of Israel, says the Lord? Did I not bring Israel out of the land of Egypt, and the foreigners from Cappadocia, and the Syrians from the pit? Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the kingdom of sinners, and I will take it away from the face of the earth. Nevertheless I will not take away the house of Jacob to the end, says the Lord. […]

But everyone who is Israel, who once saw God with his mind and was brought out of Egypt, if, desiring the vices of Egypt and the pleasures of the world, he returns not only into Egypt but into Ethiopia, in which whoever is, according to Jeremiah, cannot change his skin, is saved by the coming of Christ, and there is fulfilled in him what is written: Ethiopia shall hasten its hands to God. And when he has worshipped him, it will be said of him: Before him the Ethiopians shall fall down. And when they have fallen down, and have brought victims to the Lord from there, from beyond the rivers of Ethiopia, they will be able to say: I am black and beautiful, because the sun has discolored me. […]

The whole understanding of this passage which I have set forth, and of everything contained in this section, I will sum up in a brief discourse, up to the place where it is written: Who say, Evil will not draw near, and will not come upon us, so that we may be able to know what is said: I, the Lord God Almighty, from whom nothing can be hidden, who touch the earth and it shall be moved; who build my ascent in heaven; who call the waters of the sea and pour them out upon the face of the earth; whose name is the Lord; I who am the creator of all, formed all the nations from the same clay and begot them with an equal lot. […]

9:8.t: For the eyes of the Lord are upon all the sinning kingdoms, which the devil showed to the Lord, and of which the Apostle says: Let not sin reign in your mortal body, so that you obey its desires. Nevertheless, although he visits sinners with the rod, and crushes and strikes those who have remained in sin, he does not allow to perish for ever those souls which are called the house of Jacob, and supplant sin, and overcome in the contest, and seize the heel of the bloodstained brother.

9:9.t: For behold, I will command, and I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations, as it is shaken in a sieve, and not a pebble shall fall upon the earth. All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, who say: It will not draw near, and evil will not come upon us. LXX: For behold, I give command, and I will winnow the house of Israel among all the nations, as it is winnowed with a winnowing fan, and no crushing shall fall upon the earth. All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, who say: It will not draw near, nor will evils come upon us. […]

So too the Lord has scattered the wretched house of Israel through the whole world, and shaken it in a sieve, and winnowed it with a shovel; and while the pebbles and little stones do not fall upon the earth, those will die by the sword who, on account of their filth and dust, are called the sinners of the people. And they will suffer this because they do not believe the prophecies of the prophets, nor think that the things which the Lord threatens through them will come. And though they promise themselves prosperity, they will afterwards endure evils; while, on the other side, the saints fear and do not sin, and therefore by no means die by the sword, because they said: Evils will draw near to us, and the punishments which our sins have deserved will come upon us; […]

9:10.t: This is the sword, and this is the broadsword and the sword (framea), of which the Lord also speaks to the Father in Psalm 21 (22): Deliver my soul from the sword and my only one from the hand of the dog. Of this broadsword it is also written in Amos the prophet: All the sinners of the earth shall die by the sword. This cannot stand at all according to the letter, for many sinners perish by shipwreck, others by poison; these are choked by water, those a fire consumes. But by this sword and this broadsword all sinners perish, and the Ethiopians of black color too, of whom Zephaniah testifies with his sacred mouth, saying: But you also, Ethiopians, shall be slain by my sword.

9:11.t: After him James spoke as follows: "Men, brethren, Simon hath declared how God did purpose to take from among the Gentiles a people for His name. And thus do the words of the prophets agree, as it is written, After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down; and I will build the ruins thereof, and I will set it up: that the residue of men may seek after the Lord, and all the Gentiles, among whom my name has been invoked, saith the Lord, doing these things. Known from eternity is His work to God. Wherefore I for my part give judgment, that we trouble not them who from among the Gentiles are turned to God: but that it be enjoined them, that they do abstain from the vanities of idols, and from fornication, and from blood; […]

What then was the tabernacle in which He dwelt? Hear the Prophet say; "I will raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen." It was fallen indeed, our nature had fallen an incurable fall, and needed only that mighty Hand. There was no possibility of raising it again, had not He who fashioned it at first stretched forth to it His Hand, and stamped it new with His Image, by the regeneration of water and the Spirit. And observe I pray you, the awful and ineffable nature of the mystery. He inhabits this tabernacle for ever, for He clothed Himself with our flesh, not as again to leave it, but always to have it with Him. […]

And, not to put off with a long discourse the rule for these promises: both in this prophet and in the others, whatever is proclaimed about the building of Jerusalem and of the temple, and about the blessedness of all things, the Jews promise themselves with a vain expectation for the end of time, and they speak of it as to be fulfilled carnally. But we, who follow not the letter that kills but the spirit that gives life, prove that these things are already accomplished in the Church, and are fulfilled daily in individuals, who, falling through sin, are rebuilt through repentance.

In that day I will raise up the tabernacle of David that has fallen, and I will rebuild the openings of its walls, and what had collapsed I will restore, and I will rebuild it as in the days of old, that they may possess the remnant of Idumea, and all the nations, because my name has been invoked upon them, says the Lord who does these things. LXX: In that day I will raise up the tabernacle of David that had fallen, and I will rebuild what had collapsed, and what has been undermined I will raise up, and I will restore them as the days of old, that the rest of men may seek me, and all the Gentiles upon whom my name has been invoked, says the Lord who does all these things. […]

The tent of David means the race of the Jews. It must be known that after Cyrus had freed Israel from captivity, they returned to Judea and built the temple of God. Then, after they had again fortified the cities that had been destroyed before, they lived in security day by day for a long time. While such is the factual reference in the passage, the deeper meaning closer to reality would be in Christ. For since, as I said, Christ came back to life; for the Father raised the tent of David, and rebuilt its ruins, a great and abundant participation in spiritual goods has come upon all people, both Greeks and Jews; "For God is one, who has justified the circumcision by faith, and the uncircumcision through faith." […]

In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old, that the rest of men and all the nations may enquire who have been called by my name, saith the Lord who doeth these things. A passage of which James the Apostle makes mention in the Acts of the Apostles.

9:12.t: "After this I will return, and rebuild the tabernacle of David which is fallen down." But if one would look into the matter closely, the kingdom of David does in fact now stand, his Offspring reigning everywhere. For what is the good of the buildings and the city, with none obeying there? And what is the harm arising from the destruction of the city, when all are willing to give their very souls? There is that come which is more illustrious than David: in all parts of the world is he now sung. This has come to pass: if so, then must this also come to pass, "And I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up:" to what end? "that the residue of men may seek the Lord, and all the Gentiles, upon whom My Name is called." […]

But if we choose to read according to the LXX: That the rest of men may seek me, and all the Gentiles upon whom my name has been invoked, we ought to take as the rest of men those who believed from the Jewish people, and who, like little stones, did not fall through the sieve, nor were cast out with the dust and the chaff and the filth. For a remnant will be saved at the beginning of the faith, and at the end of the world, so that when the fullness of the Gentiles has come in, then all Israel may be saved. And the name of the Lord which is invoked upon the remnant and upon all the Gentiles is that of which the Savior says: Father, I have revealed your name to men.

9:13.t: Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and the ploughman shall overtake the reaper, and the treader of the grape him who sows the seed. And the mountains shall drip sweetness and all the hills shall be tilled. And I will turn back the captivity of my people Israel, and they shall build the deserted cities, and they shall dwell in them, and they shall plant vineyards, and they shall drink their wine, and they shall make gardens, and they shall eat their fruits. And I will plant them upon their own soil, and I will not uproot them any more from their land which I have given them, says the Lord your God. LXX: Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and the threshing shall overtake the vintage, and the grape shall change its colour at the sowing. […]

And the mountains drip sweetness. Therefore, the mountains, as it seems, here he calls the churches of Christ, on account of the loftiness of the doctrines in them, and the excellence of their piety towards God, and because the mountains appear to be covered with various plants, while the churches of Christ have countless heads of saints, like cedars and the tallest trees, which are established by the outlets of spiritual waters. But just as in the most wooded of mountains, swarms of bees flying about produce the sweet and precious honey; so again also in the churches, those who are more distinguished than others and more mature in virtue and understanding, collecting the sweet honey of the teaching about Christ, practically make it drip even into the hearts of others. […]

9:14.t: Then, if anyone is a captive through unbelief, and has not yet believed in the name of the Lord, and is of the remnant of Israel, once his people, he will return to the faith of Christ, so that what he had heard in the prophets he may hold in the Gospel. And these mountains which will drip sweetness, and the hills which have been planted, after the Lord has turned back the captivity of his people Israel, will build cities that were before deserted, and will dwell in them, so that each city that has been built may say: I am a strong city, a city that is besieged, and the one of which the Lord speaks in the Gospel: A city set upon a mountain cannot be hidden. And in the psalms it is said: The rush of the river makes glad the city of God. […]

9:15.t: And when the mountains and hills have done all these things, dripping sweetness, and building cities, and dwelling in them, planting vineyards, and drinking their wine, making gardens, and eating their fruits, then the Lord will plant the planters themselves upon their own land, of which it is said: I believe that I shall see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living, and in the Gospel: Blessed are the meek, for they shall possess the land. And after he has planted them, and made them firm with a root driven deep, he will not uproot them any more from the land which he had given them. From this we understand that the Church, until the end of the world, is indeed shaken by persecutions, but can by no means be overthrown; tempted, not overcome. […]

And that the God of all has restored our captivity, no one would doubt. For Christ proclaimed "release to the captives," and He rescued from the greed of the devil the whole world under heaven. Then indeed, then, like farmers, we became caretakers of all the spiritual fruitfulness, we planted gardens and vineyards, and we shall eat their fruit. For we shall receive the rewards for our labors, and we shall also gather the fruits of equity. And that we shall have an unshakable dwelling with God, and that no one could cast out those who are in the lots once given by him, he will make clear by saying, "I will plant them upon their land which I have given them, says the Lord God." […]
